plain_text:
No amount of alcohol is "safe" or beneficial for your
health. In fact, alcohol's harmful effects (such as risk
of developing certain cancers) start at fewer than
one drink per day. Some people should not drink
at all, including:
semantic_text: No amount of alcohol is "safe" or beneficial for your health. In fact, alcohol's harmful effects (such as risk of developing certain cancers) start at fewer than one drink per day. Some people should not drink at all, including:

plain_text:
■ People under the legal drinking age of 21
■ People with certain medical conditions
■ People who are pregnant or who may
become pregnant
semantic_text: ■ People under the legal drinking age of 21 ■ People with certain medical conditions ■ People who are pregnant or who may become pregnant

plain_text:
Drinking alcohol during pregnancy can lead to
symptoms of fetal alcohol spectrum disorders (FASD).
FASD can cause a range of neurodevelopmental and
physical effects in the child after birth.
semantic_text: Drinking alcohol during pregnancy can lead to symptoms of fetal alcohol spectrum disorders (FASD). FASD can cause a range of neurodevelopmental and physical effects in the child after birth.

plain_text:
Mixing alcohol and medicines can be harmful.


If you are on any medications, talk to your health


care provider about how alcohol may affect them.

plain_text:
Binge drinking is drinking enough alcohol to raise
one's BAC to 0.08% or above. Women typically reach
this level after about four drinks and men after about
five drinks in two hours. Binge drinking—and heavy
drinking—is a type of alcohol misuse (a spectrum
of risky alcohol-related behaviors).
semantic_text: Binge drinking is drinking enough alcohol to raise one's BAC to 0.08% or above. Women typically reach this level after about four drinks and men after about five drinks in two hours. Binge drinking—and heavy drinking—is a type of alcohol misuse (a spectrum of risky alcohol-related behaviors).

plain_text:
Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a chronic brain disorder
that makes it difficult to control alcohol use, even when it's
causing problems. AUD can be mild, moderate, or severe.
semantic_text: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a chronic brain disorder that makes it difficult to control alcohol use, even when it's causing problems. AUD can be mild, moderate, or severe.

plain_text:
Alcohol misuse at an early age increases the risk of
developing AUD. Genetics or a family history of alcohol
misuse increases that risk as well. Childhood trauma,
mental health issues, and stress can also lead people to
begin drinking or drink more than usual.
semantic_text: Alcohol misuse at an early age increases the risk of developing AUD. Genetics or a family history of alcohol misuse increases that risk as well. Childhood trauma, mental health issues, and stress can also lead people to begin drinking or drink more than usual.

plain_text:
But there is good news! No matter how severe the
problem may seem, evidence-based treatment can help
people with AUD recover.
semantic_text: But there is good news! No matter how severe the problem may seem, evidence-based treatment can help people with AUD recover.

plain_text:
While there is no one-size-fits-all method for recovering
from AUD, there are lots of effective treatment options.
Some examples include behavioral treatments, support
groups, and FDA-approved medications. NIAAA can help
people find information and resources about AUD and
treatments that might work best for them.

plain_text:
■ Rethinking Drinking is a series of self-guided questions
to help you understand your relationship with alcohol
and change your drinking habits.
■ The NIAAA Alcohol Treatment Navigator is an online
tool to help you understand AUD and how to treat
it. It can also find treatment options by health care
provider, location, and method—both virtual and
in person.
